Simple-layer variables (shortcuts)

Source: R/simple_v2.R
omop_ever.Rd

Each shortcut returns an ordinary language-2 variable (omop_variable(event = omop_event(table, concepts, ...), reducer = omop_reduce(...))); its name comes from the list it is placed in (baseline = list(hba1c = omop_value_at_index(...))). The windows are relative to the index date: before = n is omop_window(-n, 0), after = n is omop_window(1, n), window is any omop_window; the three are mutually exclusive, and without any of them the window is any time up to and including the index date (omop_window(NULL, 0)). Inf leaves the far side unbounded.

Usage

omop_ever(
  table,
  concepts = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  ...
)

omop_count(
  table,
  concepts = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  distinct = "row",
  ...
)

omop_first_value(
  table,
  concepts,
  value = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  window = NULL
)

omop_last_value(
  table,
  concepts,
  value = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  window = NULL
)

omop_mean_value(
  table,
  concepts,
  value = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  window = NULL
)

omop_min_value(
  table,
  concepts,
  value = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  window = NULL
)

omop_max_value(
  table,
  concepts,
  value = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  window = NULL
)

omop_value_at_index(table, concepts, tolerance = c(-90, 30), unit = NULL)

omop_days_since(table, concepts)

omop_days_until(table, concepts)

omop_first_date(table, concepts)

omop_last_date(table, concepts)

Arguments

table

OMOP table name, or an omop_event / omop_era (then concepts, unit, value and ... are not used).

concepts

Concept IDs, an omop_concept_set, the name of a registry concept set, or NULL for every row of the table.

before, after

Days before (up to and including the index date) or after (from the day after the index date); Inf for no limit.

window

An omop_window.

...

Further omop_event arguments (descendants, mapped, exclude, where, visit, value, unit, concept_col, end, name, on_missing_table).

distinct

What omop_count() counts: "row", "day", "visit" or "concept".

value

Numeric value column of the event (default: the table's value role, value_as_number).

unit

A unit concept ID (restriction) or an omop_unit (conversion).

tolerance

Window c(start, end) around the index date.

Value

An omop_variable.

Details

  • omop_ever(): 1 if the event occurs in the window, else 0 (reducer binary).

  • omop_count(): number of rows (or distinct days, visits, concepts) in the window.

  • omop_first_value(), omop_last_value(), omop_mean_value(), omop_min_value(), omop_max_value(): the normalised value of the first / last row in the window, or its mean, minimum or maximum.

  • omop_value_at_index(): the value closest to the index date within tolerance days (reducer closest_value).

  • omop_days_since() / omop_days_until(): days from the last row on or before / the first row on or after the index date.

  • omop_first_date() / omop_last_date(): day of the first / last row at any time, relative to the index date.

A numeric unit = U restricts the event to rows recorded in unit U (unit_concept_id == U); it never converts. Give an omop_unit to convert values to one unit.

See also

omop_study, omop_reduce

Examples

omop_ever("condition_occurrence", 201826, descendants = TRUE, before = 365)
omop_count("visit_occurrence", 9201, before = 365)
omop_value_at_index("measurement", 3004410, unit = 8554)
